terms.comment: For a Roman it was the other language: utraque lingua, both languages, is Greek and Latin (see language).

evidence: Quint. 1.1.12: ā sermōne Graecō puerum incipere mālō
Plaut. Merc. 9: Graecē haec vocātur Emporos

terms.gloss: Greek letters: the language and its literature as a study
evidence: Cic. Sen. 26: litterās Graecās senex didicī
terms.comment: To learn Greek is litterās Graecās discere: Cato learned it as an old man (Cic. Sen. 26; Quint. 12.11.23).

phrases.latin: Graecē haec vocātur Emporos Philēmōnis, eadem Latīnē Mercātor Maccī Titī
phrases.english: In Greek this play is called Philemon’s Emporos; in Latin it is the Mercator of Titus Maccius

phrases.latin: Graeca leguntur in omnibus ferē gentibus, Latīna suīs fīnibus exiguīs sānē continentur
phrases.english: Greek is read among almost every people, while Latin is kept within its own borders, and narrow ones

phrases.latin: et ego fēcī quī litterās Graecās senex didicī
phrases.english: and so did I, who learned Greek as an old man
